headline: Splicing benchmarks, dual-coding exons and nonsense constraint refine RNA regulation
label: Rna Regulation And Profiling Methods
summary: Benchmarks of splicing models and genome-wide exon studies now test how well sequence and RBP features explain splicing outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is splicing as a sequence-encoded regulatory layer, examined through predictive modelling, genome-wide annotation and population constraint. The items are heterogeneous, but splicing links them. A benchmark of foundation and deep learning models (SegmentNT, Enformer, Borzoi, SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, STEP2h) evaluates splice site and exon annotation. A genome-wide map of 1,296 human genes with dual-coding regions arising from alternative splicing reports that these regions are conserved in mice and often truncating. An NMD-informed regional nonsense constraint metric across 730,947 individuals flags 2764 genes and 22 candidate disease genes. Neuron versus glia exon inclusion is predicted from RBP binding and sequence, and neuronal splicing is found to be less sequence-dependent. What is new is explicit testing of how far sequence-based and RBP-informed models capture splicing outcomes, alongside functional consequences of splicing-derived transcript variation.
